types.description: Registry anchor for the declared API surface (ADR-0030, ADR-0054): not authorable. The `api` subtype axis is the interaction model, never the protocol; protocol lives in `binding.*` on each operation.

A named, packaged request/response surface whose children are operations (ADR-0030). It is a wire contract: two of them (`v1`, `v2`) may declare the same operation side by side. The code behind it is one service per metadata package, whose surface is the package's operations (ADR-0067). Experimental since 1.3.0: the shape may change in a MINOR, including removals and renames (docs/compatibility-policy.md).
types.whenToUse: The application does something beyond derived CRUD: a named command (approve, cancel, import) or a named query (my open requests). Declare it here so its input, output, permission and business errors are part of the model. A plain lifecycle needs no api.operational at all: each transition nobody claims derives its own command.
types.rules: Children are `operation.command` and `operation.query`. Lives at the document root. Declares no fields, sources or identities: shapes are referenced, never defined, by the surface. Operation names are compared without case, are unique across every API of one package, except one operation declared identically in two APIs, such as a versioned API beside its successor (one operation declared twice in one API merges), and may not be create, get, list, update or delete in any case (ERR_TRANSITION_NAME_COLLISION). Two declared bindings may not share a method and path (ERR_BINDING_PATH_MISMATCH).

types.description: Registry anchor for the attributes every operation shares (ADR-0054): not authorable.

children.description: Optional protocol bindings. Only needed to override the derived method and path.

children.name: inputRef
children.description: The `object.value` this operation takes as its input (ADR-0030). Absent on an operation whose only parameter is the target's borrowed key. Anything other than an `object.value` is ERR_OPERATION_SHAPE.

children.name: outputRef
children.description: The object this operation returns: an `object.projection`, `object.entity` or `object.value`. Which projection a query returns is the author's choice among several over one entity, so it cannot be computed. Anything else is ERR_OPERATION_SHAPE.

children.name: objectRef
children.description: The entity this operation acts on, declared only when it cannot be derived. It is derived from the input value when its fields `extend` every primary key field of exactly one entity, each once, else from the output's base entity; an input that borrows part of a key, one key field twice, or the keys of two entities derives nothing, so declare it. Declared and derivable, the two must agree (ERR_OPERATION_TARGET_MISMATCH). It must name an `object.entity` (ERR_OPERATION_TARGET_UNRESOLVED).

children.name: permission
children.description: The permission name the generated shell asks the project's policy about before anything is written. A key into grant data (who holds it is data, what the policy decides is code), so it is never derived from the operation's name: a rename would silently move access. A dotted identifier path such as `purchasing.approve`; a package prefix may use `::` (ERR_BAD_ATTR_VALUE otherwise). Absent and not @public: the shell uses the derived name `<package>.<operation>`, with the package of the operation's API, and `verify` advises or requires an explicit one (setting `rules.permissions.names`). Several operations may share one.

children.name: public
children.description: The shell calls no permission check. Authentication is the transport's job and is unaffected. Absent means checked. Declaring it with @permission is ERR_PERMISSION_PUBLIC_CONFLICT.

types.description: A named operation that changes state. Takes an `object.value` (ADR-0030). Its body is hand-written; the generated shell around it loads the row, checks the permission and the current state, runs the body, and makes the guarded update in one transaction (ADR-0066). Experimental since 1.3.0: the shape may change in a MINOR, including removals and renames (docs/compatibility-policy.md).
types.whenToUse: A business action with its own name, input and rules: approve, cancel, transfer. A command that moves a lifecycle names the transitions it may make in @transitions; its body decides which one applies.

children.name: transitions
children.description: The lifecycle moves this command may make: names of `transition.action` nodes on its target entity (ERR_OPERATION_UNKNOWN_TRANSITION otherwise). A fact of the business the model cannot compute. A transition a command lists gets no derived command of its own. Listing any requires a target (ERR_OPERATION_TARGET_UNRESOLVED).

children.name: errors
children.description: The business failures the hand-written body may return, each a lower snake case code (`insufficient_funds`). They name the wire error, the OpenAPI document and the typed result; the shell refuses an undeclared one. A code that is not lower snake case, appears twice, or is one the route answers itself (not_found, forbidden, invalid_transition, transition_condition_failed, state_managed, validation, invalid_json, invalid_id, method_not_allowed, constraint_violation, internal) is ERR_BAD_ATTR_VALUE.

types.description: A named operation that reads. Returns an `object.projection` (or an entity or value). It changes nothing. Experimental since 1.3.0: the shape may change in a MINOR, including removals and renames (docs/compatibility-policy.md).
types.whenToUse: A read with its own name and shape beyond derived get and list: my open requests, the dashboard summary.

children.name: many
children.description: The query returns a list and takes the filter, sort and paging contract. Not implied by the projection, so declared. Absent means one row. Legal on a query only.

types.description: Registry anchor for protocol bindings (ADR-0030, ADR-0054): not authorable.

The HTTP method and path of an operation, declared only to override the derived ones. A query is `GET`, a command `POST`; the path is `/<collection>/{id}/<operation-kebab>` for an operation with a target key and `/<collection>/<operation-kebab>` without one. Most models never write it. Experimental since 1.3.0: the shape may change in a MINOR, including removals and renames (docs/compatibility-policy.md).
types.whenToUse: An operation must keep a method or path the derived one would not give it, such as an existing public URL.

children.name: method
children.description: The HTTP method. Absent: GET for a query, POST for a command.

children.name: path
children.description: A path template. Its `{name}` placeholders must be exactly the target's primary key fields when the operation is keyed, and there must be none when it is not; two declared bindings of one API may not share the method and path (ERR_BINDING_PATH_MISMATCH).
